title: A sequence in Sequential Function Chart: fill, then mix
summary: Complete a Sequential Function Chart with three steps by adding the missing timed transition, and check that the valve and the mixer never run together.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not show how much a real tank holds, how well it mixes or how fast a real valve moves.
objectives: Read a Sequential Function Chart as steps that are active one at a time, actions that run while their step is active, and transitions that move the activity.
Add a timed transition that uses the elapsed time of a step.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/FillMix.sfc.json the steps IDLE, FILL and MIX are drawn with their actions, and so are the transitions from IDLE to FILL (Start) and from MIX back to IDLE (after a time). The transition out of FILL is missing. Make the sequence leave FILL for MIX once FILL has been active for {{t:50}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: The sequence runs IDLE, FILL, MIX and back to IDLE on each Start, with one step active at a time.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Start is pressed at {{t:10}} ms. The step changes on the scan after the condition becomes true. Predict Valve and Mixer at {{t:20}}, {{t:80}} and {{t:140}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:FillMix.Valve=true,FillMix.Mixer=false@20|Valve ON}} at {{t:20}} ms; {{v:FillMix.Valve=false,FillMix.Mixer=true@80|Mixer ON}} at {{t:80}} ms; {{v:FillMix.Valve=false,FillMix.Mixer=false@140|both OFF}} at {{t:140}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Complete the chart, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting chart has the three steps and two of the three transitions, so FILL never ends: the valve stays open and MIX never runs. The valve must close and the mixer must start once FILL has been active for {{t:50}} ms, and the rest of the sequence must stay as it is: MIX still returns to IDLE, which waits for the next Start.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson and lists every assertion that failed.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named FillMix and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare {{t:70}}, {{t:80}} and {{t:130}} ms: the valve closes and the mixer starts in the same scan at {{t:80}} ms, and the mixer runs for {{t:50}} ms before the sequence returns to IDLE.
stages.checkpoint: The valve and the mixer are never ON together. A second Start at {{t:160}} ms repeats the cycle.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Which step is active while the valve is open, and why can only one be active at a time? A real tank leaves FILL when a level switch says it is full, not after a time: what would change in the chart?
stages.checkpoint: Each action writes both outputs, so a step defines the whole output state and the sequence cannot leave an output on by accident. With a level switch only the condition of the transition out of FILL changes: it reads the switch instead of the clock of the step.

hints.text: A transition has a source step, a target step and a condition. The transition out of MIX already leaves after a time, because its condition reads the clock of its own step, step_mix.T. FILL needs the same kind of transition, to MIX.
Add a transition with fromStep step_fill, toStep step_mix and the condition step_fill.T >= T#50ms.

faultCases: The starting chart has the three steps and two of the three transitions, so FILL never ends: the valve stays open and MIX never runs.
